messages:
sara: quick follow-up to the attn-selector RFC — ran a small perf + correctness sweep. want to capture what we learned and possible next steps.

sara: summary: per-request routing (route entire request to either grouped-query or multi-query kernel) means simpler runtime, fewer context switches, lower KV cache churn. downside: if a batch contains mixed shapes we get suboptimal batching and more idle GPU time.

sara: put a tiny decision prototype in runtime/attn/splitter. pseudocode:```
fn pick_path(req) -> Path {
  if req.num_queries > 8 || req.seq_len < 128 {
    return MultiQuery
  }
  if req.prefers_low_latency && model.supports_gq {
    return GroupedQuery
  }
  // fallback to cost-estimate based on tokens and cache-hit
  return cost_estimate(req) < threshold ? GroupedQuery : MultiQuery
}
```

sara: experiment: 1k-simulated-user traces, 90/10 mix short/long. per-request routing improved p95 latency by ~8% for short requests, but tail throughput dropped ~6% under high concurrency.

mike: interesting. did you try hybrid: pick per-request but allow an intra-batch splitter to move small runs into GQ buckets?

sara: yeah — prototype allowed a secondary re-shuffle stage inside the enqueue path. that reduced waste but added 1 mutex and a copy step, and under 99% of cases cost > benefit unless the batch had >30% mixed shapes.

anita: from a kernel-selection API POV, would we expose two decisions: static_path_hint + runtime_rebucket_hint? that keeps runtime deterministic for Dedicated users.

ryan: +1 to deterministic hints. Also worried about KV cache invalidations if we switch mid-request (token-level decisions). any numbers on cache-miss amplification?

sara: token-level switching (i.e., start in MQA, then switch to GQA) blew up KV cache misses by ~3-4x in traces where prompts reused prefixes across requests. so not great for latency-sensitive workloads.

dom: what about a sticky-session policy: route requests based on recent history for that client id, with TTL? could avoid flipflop for chat sessions.

mike: sticky-session sounds reasonable but we need eviction heuristics. LRU per-GPU? global tracker? might be heavy.

anita: maybe make sticky-session opt-in per-model-deployment. enterprise customers can toggle. default runtime behavior remains per-request with optional rebucket.

ryan: ops question: how does this affect tracing and observability? if we rebucket or sticky-route we need to tag spans with chosen path and reason. otherwise debugging is a nightmare.

sara: agreed — added a proposal: every request gets fields: chosen_path, decision_reason_code, rebucketed_flag. these flow into span + route metrics. small change but crucial.

ci-bot: build/attn-splitter-proto #42 passed (linux/gpu unit tests) :white_check_mark:

dom: next steps I see: (1) land path_hint API (2) implement opt-in sticky-session TTL (3) wire observability tags (4) run 48h canary on dedicated pool. anyone want to take (2)?

mike: I can own sticky-session; will prototype LRU with per-GPU sharding and async eviction.

anita: I can do the API + metrics wiring. will draft a tiny RFC addendum.

sara: awesome. mike + anita — sync tomorrow 10am. i'll push the experimental traces and perf graphs to the thread in a bit. :thumbsup:

ryan: thanks — feel like this is a pragmatic middle ground between full token-level switching and naive per-request routing.

sara: exactly — goal is predictable perf for customers while recovering some batching efficiency when mixed workloads occur.

dom: 👍 prioritize observability before canary. last thing we need is a silent regression at scale.

sara: noted. will add a checklist in the RFC addendum.
